1.w: The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:

2.w: To learn wisdom and moral instruction, to discern wise counsel.

3.w: To receive moral instruction in skillful living, with righteousness, justice, and equity.

4.w: To impart shrewdness to the morally naive, a discerning plan to the young person.

5.w: (Let the wise also hear and gain instruction, and let the discerning acquire guidance!)

6.w: To discern the meaning of a proverb and a parable, the sayings of the wise and their riddles.

7.w: Fearing the Lord is the beginning of discernment, but fools have despised wisdom and moral instruction.

8.w: Listen, my child, to the instruction from your father, and do not forsake the teaching from your mother.

9.w: For they will be like an elegant garland on your head, and like pendants around your neck.

10.w: My child, if sinners try to entice you, do not consent!

11.w: If they say, “Come with us! We will lie in wait to shed blood; we will ambush an innocent person capriciously.

12.w: We will swallow them alive like Sheol, those full of vigor like those going down to the Pit.

13.w: We will seize all kinds of precious wealth; we will fill our houses with plunder.

14.w: Join with us! We will all share equally in what we steal.”

15.w: My child, do not go down their way, withhold yourself from their path;

16.w: for they are eager to inflict harm, and they hasten to shed blood.

17.w: Surely it is futile to spread a net in plain sight of any bird,

18.w: but these men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives!

19.w: Such are the ways of all who gain profit unjustly; it takes away the life of those who obtain it!

20.w: Wisdom calls out in the street, she shouts loudly in the plazas;

21.w: at the head of the noisy streets she calls, in the entrances of the gates in the city she utters her words:

22.w: “How long will you simpletons love naiveté? How long have mockers delighted in mockery? And how long will fools hate knowledge?

23.w: You should respond to my rebuke. Then I would pour out my thoughts to you; I would make my words known to you.

24.w: However, because I called but you refused to listen, because I stretched out my hand but no one was paying attention,

25.w: and you neglected all my advice, and did not comply with my rebuke,

26.w: so I myself will laugh when disaster strikes you; I will mock when what you dread comes,

27.w: when what you dread comes like a whirlwind, and disaster strikes you like a devastating storm, when distressing trouble comes on you.

28.w: Then they will call to me, but I will not answer; they will diligently seek me, but they will not find me.

29.w: Because they hated moral knowledge and did not choose to fear the Lord ,

30.w: they did not comply with my advice; they spurned all my rebuke.

31.w: Therefore they will eat from the fruit of their way, and they will be stuffed full of their own counsel.

32.w: For the waywardness of the simpletons will kill them, and the careless ease of fools will destroy them.

33.w: But the one who listens to me will live in security and will be at ease from the dread of harm.”
